subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw make per-agent workspace confinement a default security boundary, keep it opt-in through existing sandbox/`tools.fs.workspaceOnly`, or split filesystem tools from exec and OS-user isolation?
rationale: The answer changes a security boundary and compatibility default for existing host workflows, and current source shows filesystem tools, exec, and sandboxing have separate enforcement paths.

options.title: Choose a staged default-boundary design
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the default posture, upgrade behavior, and separate filesystem-tool versus exec semantics before accepting a partial fix.

options.title: Keep confinement opt-in
options.body: Document `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` and sandbox modes as the supported answer, and close only after maintainers explicitly accept that the default host posture remains permissive.

options.title: Route to narrower implementation issues
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/7722 for configurable filesystem ACLs and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78965 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12505 for stronger runtime isolation, preserving this report as context.

recommendation.title: Choose a staged default-boundary design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the default posture, upgrade behavior, and separate filesystem-tool versus exec semantics before accepting a partial fix.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest combined history on the current filesystem policy default and prior related review decisions.
